hints.title: Basis of Operations
hints.text: Consider the number of independent positions where the length k inversion window can be applied.

hints.title: Linear Independence
hints.text: Each window operation is reversible and flips a unique leftmost index that cannot be affected by any window placed strictly to its right.

hints.title: Counting Distinct Configurations
hints.text: Because there are n - k + 1 independent binary choices and each distinct combination yields a unique resulting string, the total number of distinct outcomes is 2^(n - k + 1) modulo 10^9 + 7.

hints.title: Modular Exponentiation Implementation

complexity.notes: Fast modular exponentiation computes the result in logarithmic steps.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Simulating all combinations leads to exponential 2^(n-k+1) state exploration.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Recognizes that each window placement provides an independent degree of freedom in linear algebra over GF(2).
